methodological_rigor.justification: Methodologically rigorous synthetic cohort generation with clear statistical validation (stratified train-test splits, cross-validation, bootstrap confidence intervals). However, real clinical validation is limited to exploratory 60-lesion brain-metastasis comparison explicitly stated as non-validation. Complete-repair assumption between fractions acknowledged with sensitivity analysis, but represents a simplifying assumption not fully validated clinically. External validation lacking.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Primarily computational framework tested on large synthetic cohorts; limited integration of real patient data only for exploratory consistency checks. Authors explicitly state 'full clinical validation is planned.' Pathology-dependent findings may inform future clinical radiosurgery planning but lack direct clinical evidence. Radiobiological framework development is valuable but pre-clinical relative to clinical application.

reporting_quality.justification: Detailed methods section with comprehensive mathematical formulations and parameter specifications. TRIPOD elements for prediction models partially addressed. However, synthetic data generation code, radiobiological parameter sets, and machine-learning models not explicitly stated as available in repositories. Python functions described but reproducibility of full pipeline unclear without code access.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel multi-fraction extension of Jones-Hopewell radiobiological model to encompass 1-, 3-, and 5-fraction Gamma Knife treatments; first unified framework integrating mechanistic radiobiology with machine-learning outcome prediction. Demonstrates pathology-dependent utility of BED (strong in AVM, moderate in meningioma, weak in VS and BM). Mechanistic grounding combined with AI represents substantive methodological contribution beyond prior single-fraction models.

writing_presentation.justification: Technically clear with well-structured mathematical derivations and comprehensive methods. Extensive supplementary content with detailed parameter specifications. Results section is comprehensive but lengthy. Some sections overly technical for general oncology audience. Figures effectively communicate model performance and cross-pathology comparisons. Organization appropriate for specialized radiobiology/physics audience.

key_strengths: Novel unified multi-fraction radiobiological framework extending Jones-Hopewell model across fractionation schedules
Rigorous synthetic cohort validation with pathology-specific radiobiological parameters across four major Gamma Knife indications
Clear demonstration of pathology-dependent BED utility, not universal advantage
Sophisticated integration of mechanistic radiobiology with machine learning for outcome prediction
key_concerns: Limited real-patient validation; only exploratory comparison with 60 brain-metastasis cases explicitly non-validating
Complete-repair assumption between fractions represents simplification not fully validated in clinical settings
Synthetic data, while methodologically sound, lacks ground-truth biological mechanisms matching real tumors
Code and data availability not explicitly stated; reproducibility of full pipeline unclear without access to computational tools
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sophisticated computational framework with clear internal validation but insufficient external clinical validation. Appropriate for Tier 3 with major revisions requiring: (1) explicit statement of data/code availability; (2) larger real-patient cohort validation; (3) clinical outcome correlation study design.
